title: SanDisk Slips Below $815 as Analysts Split on Whether the AI Memory Trade Is Broken
text:

 Add preferred source 1 SanDisk closed at $814.56 on Nov. 19, down 1.73% and below every major moving average, leaving the stock in a confirmed downtrend despite fiscal first-quarter revenue of $11.0 billion, up 23% sequentially, and non-GAAP earnings of $49.51 a share. An eight-for-one split took effect the same day. Analyst views are split: Evercore ISI reiterated Outperform with a $2,500 target, while Zacks Research cut its rating to hold even as its own $1,881 target implies large upside. Consensus targets near $2,050 sit far above the current price, but technicals remain weak, with RSI at 35.19 and MACD negative. Binance futures positioning is heavily long, and SemiAnalysis forecasts steep declines in AI chip capital spending through 2029. Key Elements 
 SanDisk SNDK Evercore ISI Zacks Research SemiAnalysis Nvidia Binance Futures NAND flash memory S&P Global SanDisk Corp. (SNDK) closed at $814.56 on Nov. 19, down 1.73% on the session after trading in a range of $755.07 to $830.98, as the memory chipmaker's shares continued to work through a steep retracement from their highs even as sell-side coverage stayed largely constructive.
 The stock now sits below all four of its key trend lines — a 7-day simple moving average of $835.20, a 20-day SMA of $921.27, a 50-day SMA of $1,237.84 and a 200-day SMA of $1,538.34. That stack, with each shorter average below the next longer one, is the signature of a downtrend rather than a pause, and it has shifted the debate from how much upside remains to whether the recent slide is a reset or the start of something deeper.
 The fundamental picture presented by the company remains firm. In its fiscal first-quarter 2027 report released Oct. 29, SanDisk posted revenue of $11.0 billion, up 23% from the prior quarter, and non-GAAP diluted earnings of $49.51 a share. Management said it returned $5.0 billion to shareholders through buybacks during the quarter, and over the past two fiscal quarters it repurchased 6.0 million shares, roughly 4% of shares outstanding. The board also authorized up to $14 billion in additional repurchases and approved an eight-for-one forward stock split effective Nov. 19.
 That split takes effect against a backdrop of sharply divided analyst opinion on valuation. Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and a $2,500 price target on Nov. 11, arguing that investors are underestimating structural changes in SanDisk's business model; a separate note tied the thesis to multiyear supply agreements that could shield margins if flash memory pricing cools. Zacks Research, by contrast, cut its rating from "strong buy" to "hold," according to StreetInsider.com — though Zacks' own website lists the downgrade as having occurred two days earlier and carries a $1,881 target, a figure that would imply gains of roughly 150% from recent levels.
 Consensus data reflects the same tension. Analysts tracked by S&P Global show a Strong Buy rating with an average target of $2,047, a low of $870 and a high of $3,000, while a separate consensus cited by MarketBeat puts the average at $2,056.23 with a Moderate Buy rating. The gap between the lowest target and the current price is now narrow, which suggests the market has stopped treating the stock as a straightforward momentum long.

 Last close (Nov. 19) $814.56 
 24-hour range $755.07 - $830.98 
 7-day SMA $835.20 
 20-day SMA $921.27 
 50-day SMA $1,237.84 
 200-day SMA $1,538.34 
 RSI (14) 35.19 
 Immediate resistance $845.34 
 Immediate support $769.43 
 Pivot $800.20 
 Note: Moving averages and indicator readings as of the Nov. 19 session.
 Momentum gauges point to persistent weakness rather than a clean reversal. The relative strength index stands at 35.19 — close to oversold but not there yet — while MACD is negative at -120.6474. The stock is trading below the middle Bollinger Band at $921.27 with %B at 0.2848, keeping price pinned in the lower part of its recent volatility envelope. The 14-day average true range of $83.09 means intraday moves can overshoot technical levels with ease.
 On the chart, immediate resistance sits at $845.34 and a stronger ceiling at $876.11. To the downside, the first line is $769.43, with firmer support at $724.29. The $800.20 pivot is the level the market is currently trying to hold.
 Derivatives positioning offers a counterweight to the bearish price trend without confirming it. On Binance perpetual futures, the 8-hour funding rate was flat at 0.0000%, open interest stood at 277,103.25 contracts and had fallen 3.87% over 24 hours, a modest deleveraging rather than a washout. Binance global accounts were 86.0% long against 14.1% short as of 10:00 UTC on Nov. 19, with top-trader accounts at 87.6% long versus 12.3% short. The taker buy/sell ratio of 1.1667, on buy volume of 48,929 against 41,939 sold, shows aggressive buyers have not disappeared.
 Broader sector pressure has compounded the stock-specific story. Investors have been marking down AI-linked chip names on concern that demand could cool, and those worries were sharpened when semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis projected that capital spending on AI chips in 2027 would come in 19% below prior estimates, with 2028 spending 28% below expectations and 2029 spending 41% below. As one of the largest makers of NAND flash memory, SanDisk is directly exposed to that spending cycle.
 The tactical setup is now binary. A reclaim of $845.34 followed by a close above $876.11 would let the market frame the decline as consolidation within a larger re-rating. A loss of the $800.20 pivot and then failure at $769.43 would open the path toward $724.29, with the lower Bollinger Band near $682.57 acting as a broader downside reference. Until price recovers its short-term moving averages, the stock remains a rebound candidate rather than a confirmed resumption of the uptrend.
 For investors, the practical takeaway is that the bullish case now rests on earnings durability and capital returns rather than price momentum, while the bear case rests on a technical structure that has not yet repaired and an end-market outlook that at least one research firm sees deteriorating sharply into 2029.
